sections.h2: What does the Halifax County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The Halifax County Register of Deeds records, indexes and preserves real estate records, and it also keeps plats, UCC filings, vital records and miscellaneous records. The register is an elected official serving a 4-year term, and the county says the staff is an assistant and four deputies.

The counter is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., excluding holidays. The county site lists a Register of Deeds Index Search for online research. Halifax is a Coastal Plain county on the Roanoke River, formed from Edgecombe County in 1758, and its seat is the town of Halifax. The Census Bureau estimated 46,534 residents in July 2025.

sections.h2: How far back do Halifax County land records go?
sections.html:
Hard-copy indexes cover real estate records back to 1732, which predates the county itself. Online, the Register of Deeds Index Search offers three layers, and the county lists them on its Real Estate Records page:

  • Real property indexes and record images from 1976 to the present.
  • Historical real estate indexes from 1934 to 1975.
  • Survey maps going back to 1818.

Vital records have their own reach. Marriage records start in 1825, and birth and death records start in October 1913. Anything older than 1976 on a parcel means working from the historical or hard-copy indexes.

sections.h2: Why does the Halifax County Tax Collector sign off before a deed records?
sections.html:
The county commissioners directed the Register of Deeds, effective January 1, 2016, to refuse any deed transferring real property unless the Tax Collector has certified that no delinquent ad valorem taxes, or other taxes the collector is charged to collect, are a lien on the described parcel.

The deed must reach the Tax Collector's office between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. so the staff can research the parcel. That office is Tax Administration at 357 Ferrell Lane, Halifax, phone 252-583-2121. Plan the certification before the register's counter, not after, since a deed without it is turned away. Our Halifax County property tax guide covers rates, appeals and relief programs.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record in Halifax County?
sections.html:
The county's fiscal year 2026-27 fee schedule lists a $26 charge for the first 15 pages of an instrument and $64 for the first 35 pages of a deed of trust or mortgage, each with $4 per added page. Those figures follow the uniform recording fees set in state law.

Halifax County Register of Deeds fees, fiscal year 2026-27 schedule

Source: Halifax County Schedule of Fees, fiscal year 2026-27. The same schedule charges $10 for each added index reference on an assignment, $2 per party beyond 20 distinct parties, and 25 cents per page for photocopies and scanned images. State law collects these fees before filing and calls the list complete and exclusive.

sections.h2: How much is the Halifax County deed stamp tax and who pays it?
sections.html:
The county schedule shows an excise stamp tax of $1.00 on each $500, or fraction of $500, of the consideration or value conveyed. That matches the state statute, which puts the tax on the transferor and requires it to be paid to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

Half of the collection goes into the county general fund, and the other half, less refunds and allowance, goes to the state Department of Revenue each month. The county budget ordinance for 2026-27 lists $353,500 for the Register of Deeds under other taxes and licenses. For a parcel that lies in two or more counties, the tax goes to the county that holds the greater share of the value. Ask the closing attorney for the exact stamp tax figure before settlement.

sections.h2: What recording rules matter for Halifax County contracts for deed and other transfers?
sections.html:
A deed, an option and a lease longer than three years do not hold against lien creditors or later buyers for value until registered in the county where the land lies. Priority follows the order and time of registration.

Seller-financed deals fall under Chapter 47H when the buyer makes five or more payments beyond the down payment and the seller keeps title to a one to four family home or manufactured home priced at $5,000 or more. Such a contract must be written, signed and acknowledged. The seller must record the contract or a Memorandum of a Contract for Deed within five business days, and the buyer may cancel until midnight of the third business day after signing. Forfeiture needs a written notice that gives at least 30 days to cure.

Have an attorney draft any land contract and confirm the recording.

sections.h2: Where do Halifax County tax foreclosure sales fit in the records?
sections.html:
A tax foreclosure sale ends in a deed, so the register eventually records the result. The county posts notices on its Tax Foreclosures page, and sales take place in the lower lobby of the Halifax County Courthouse. Each bid is open to a 10-day upset bid, and properties sell as is.

The county warns that sales are subject to outstanding taxes, assessments and liens of anyone who was not named as a defendant, and advises bidders to get a title examination first. If you own a house with a tax foreclosure pending, a sale before the court's hearing keeps control of the price in your hands, and the register will record the deed once the tax certification is on file.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Halifax County homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 25,078 housing units in July 2025 and 20,383 households for 2020 to 2024. The owner-occupied rate is 62.9%, the median owner-occupied value is $106,200, and median gross rent is $813.

The median household income is $45,590 in 2024 dollars and 25.2% of residents are 65 or older. Only 75 building permits were issued in 2025, and 88.9% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. The county covers 723.74 square miles of land with about 67 residents per square mile in 2020.

faqs.q: What are the hours of the Halifax County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., excluding holidays. The tax certification that a deed needs before recording is handled at the Tax Collector's office between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Halifax County?
faqs.a: The county fee schedule for 2026-27 lists $26 for the first 15 pages of an instrument and $4 for each added page, plus $25 if the form is non-standard. The seller also pays excise stamp tax of $1.00 per $500 of value.

faqs.q: Why was my Halifax County deed refused for recording?
faqs.a: One cause is a missing certification from the Tax Collector. Since January 1, 2016, the register cannot accept a deed transferring real property unless delinquent taxes have been cleared and certified. Take the deed to Tax Administration first.

faqs.q: How far back do Halifax County real estate records go?
faqs.a: Hard-copy indexes reach back to 1732. Online, property indexes and images cover 1976 to the present, historical indexes cover 1934 to 1975, and survey maps date from 1818.

faqs.q: Does Halifax County charge to record a mortgage satisfaction?
faqs.a: No. The county's fee schedule lists satisfactions as no charge, and state law sets the same rule. A deed of trust itself costs $64 for the first 35 pages.
